title: Hopper GEMM: TMA, mbarrier, and wgmma
brief: Compute a TMA box address, the 128-byte swizzle that matches the box, and a wgmma descriptor. The same file carries an sm_90a TMA copy and one wgmma. Those kernels run only on an H100.
hints: box_byte_offset adds the box origin before it scales. Dimension 0 is the contiguous column: byte = (origin_col + local_col) * elem_bytes + (origin_row + local_row) * stride_bytes.
box_load returns 0 for a coordinate outside the matrix. The origin is part of the global coordinate. Using the local index alone reads the wrong tile.
swizzle_128b_byte XORs (row mod 8) into the 16-byte chunk index, bits 4 to 6 of the byte offset. XORing the row into bits 0 to 2 is a different map. Row 1, chunk 1 lands at byte 128.
choose_swizzle returns 128B, 64B, or 32B when the box's inner byte count equals that span. Any other multiple of 16 is none. A width that is not a multiple of 16 is illegal.
wgmma_descriptor stores the 128-byte mode as layout_type 1 in bits 62 to 63. That is not the driver enum, where 128B is the fourth enumerator.
predicted_ms uses the H100 SXM5 ratings, 989.4 TFLOP/s and 3350 GB/s. The kernel is not graded against that floor.
tma_copy and wgmma_64x8x16 compile with arch sm_90a. On a machine without an H100 they are skipped, and the job is not sent to the A100.
